context.description: Streaky Bay is a fishing and farming town on the west side of the Eyre Peninsula, 303 km north-west of Port Lincoln. Matthew Flinders named the bay in 1802 for the streaks of discoloured water he saw. A 350 m jetty runs out from the town centre and oysters and abalone are farmed in the bay. Coastal loops lead to blowholes and cliffs at Cape Bauer, and Murphy's Haystacks stand on farmland to the south-east.

context.description: Ceduna sits on Murat Bay on the Eyre Highway, the last major town before the Nullarbor. A 380 m jetty runs out from its foreshore, and the oyster farms of Smoky Bay lie 45 km along the coast. To the west, Penong has a roadside windmill museum, and the road south leads to the surf breaks of Cactus Beach and the salt lakes beside it. Conservation parks with mangroves and shorebird feeding grounds line the coast either side of town.

context.description: Whyalla is South Australia's steel city on the upper Spencer Gulf, built around the iron ore from nearby Iron Knob. Its maritime museum holds HMAS Whyalla, a corvette launched in 1941 that now sits two kilometres from the sea. Every winter tens of thousands of giant Australian cuttlefish gather to spawn off Point Lowly. The foreshore has a circular jetty, a marina and a beach.

context.description: Gawler Ranges National Park lies about 40 km north of the Eyre Highway, with road access from Iron Knob, Kimba, Wudinna or Minnipa. It was proclaimed in 2002 on the former Paney Station and protects crimson mallee and the yellow-footed rock-wallaby. The Organ Pipes, formed by volcanic eruptions about 1,500 million years ago, are its best-known sight, with rocky falls at Yandinga and Kolay Mirica. South of the ranges, the Wudinna area is granite country of domes such as Mount Wudinna and Pildappa Rock.
